newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - MARCH 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - MARCH 5.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Fears for the safety of the ethnic Greek minority in Albania appear to have been behind Prime Minister Costas Simitis's late night phone call to Albanian President Sali Berisha, who reassured him that Tirana did not blame the minority for the recent wave of unrest. Berisha is reported to have said he want to avoid the use of force.

--Greece has undertaken a series of initiatives through the European Union to bring about a peaceful resolution of the crisis in the neighbouring country. Simitis had a range of talks with leaders of EU partners to coordinate the EU's intervention in Albania, in line with Athens position that the crisis is not a bilateral but a Community issue.

--The government is promoting alternative forms of employment that will not see the 40-hour week or pay reduced. The idea behind the new plans is to make the working week more flexible and productive for workers and employers.
--All military units on the country's northern borders were on alert last night while the defence ministry decided to move reinforcements up to the 8th battalion, stationed in Epirus.
--Internal pressures and realignment in the conservative opposition party New Democracy as the three front-runners for president jostle for a lead.
--Today will see the election of the 1,309 delegates to the crucial New Democracy congress later this month: later today, the four candidates will be in a position to assess their strength.
--Secondary school teachers have decided on an eighth week to their strike, making the extension of the school year a definite possibility, despite opposition from students and parents.
